title: Ivo and the Veil
premise: Mirabel Quintana, a cartographer who can chart realms that exist only in ink and memory, has spent years hiding his gift behind the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things. When the crown's Veilhunt begins executing anyone with the sight, Mirabel learns the guild itself sold out its gifted members to survive—and that the failing covenant between his realm and the unmapped lands is collapsing because the last cartographer to renew it was betrayed. To stop both realms from unraveling, Mirabel must cross into the unmapped world, confront the guildmaster who traded him away, and choose between exposing the truth that will destroy the guild or preserving the lie that will doom two worlds. In the end he rewrites the covenant in his own blood and name, sacrificing his invisibility—and nearly his life—to bind the realms together openly.
about_author: Edmund Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. He writes fantasy about people who keep dangerous records.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Mirabel Quintana, POV. In the Guild of Impossible Things, Mirabel balances accounts for impossible trades while secretly sketching a map of a realm only he can see. The beat: quiet dread beneath routine, establishing his double life and the comfort he'll lose.

chapters.title: A Proclamation Nailed to Every Door
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The crown declares the Veilhunt: all with the sight must register or die. Guild members whisper; the guildmaster, Corvane, urges calm. Mirabel burns one of his maps but cannot burn them all. Beat: fear arrives, and the illusion of safety cracks.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Ash
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A hooded client commissions a map to the unmapped realm, paying in cinders that smell of home. Mirabel refuses—then recognizes the ash as coming from a village already purged. Beat: complicity; refusing the job doesn't undo what's been done.

chapters.title: What Sela Knew
chapters.summary: Sela Voss, a fellow guild clerk and Mirabel's closest friend, POV. Sela has noticed Mirabel's midnight inks glowing. She covers for him when a Veilwarden inspects the guild, lying for the first time. Beat: loyalty kindles, and she becomes complicit in his secret.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Quiet Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV (partial). Corvane reviews a secret ledger: names of gifted members already sold to the crown in exchange for the guild's charter. Mirabel's name sits at the bottom, unsent—for now. Beat: chilling pragmatism; the reader sees the betrayal before the hero does.

chapters.title: Ink That Wouldn't Dry
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. His maps begin bleeding color into the real world—a sign the covenant between realms is failing. A door in his map opens briefly, and something on the other side calls his name. Beat: wonder curdling into urgency; time is running out.

chapters.title: Sela's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Sela discovers Corvane's ledger of sold names and finds Mirabel listed. She steals the page, knowing theft means exile or worse. Beat: loyalty vs. self-preservation made literal; she chooses him over her own safety.

chapters.title: The Night of Long Knives
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Veilwardens raid the guild, armed with Corvane's list. Half the staff are taken. Mirabel survives only because Sela hides him in the map-room, inside a drawn doorway. Beat: terror and grief; the guild that sheltered him has unsheltered everyone else.

chapters.title: Through the Drawn Door
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Trapped in the map-realm between pages, Mirabel crosses fully into the unmapped world: a country stitched from forgotten geography. He meets the Warden of Margins, a creature older than the covenant. Beat: awe and displacement; belonging feels possible here, yet he's an intruder.

chapters.title: The Last Cartographer's Grave
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The Warden shows him the grave of Alderyn, the cartographer who last renewed the covenant—and reveals Alderyn was betrayed by her own guild, exactly as Mirabel is being betrayed now. Beat: history rhyming; Mirabel understands the pattern he's caught in.

chapters.title: Sela on the Run
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Hunted with the stolen ledger page as her only proof, Sela seeks the crown's own archivist, an unlikely ally who hates the Veilhunt's sloppy cruelty. Beat: desperate alliance; truth needs strange vessels.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. To reach the covenant-stone at the realm's heart, Mirabel must trade a memory to the ferryman of unmapped rivers. He gives up his memory of his mother's face. Beat: the theme made flesh—survival costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Corvane's Defense
chapters.summary: Corvane, POV. Confronted by surviving guild members, Corvane argues he saved forty lives by giving up six, and that Mirabel would have doomed them all. Some believe him. Beat: uncomfortable moral weight; the villain is half right.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Cellar
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. In the crown archives, Sela and the archivist find proof the Veilhunt was engineered by Corvane's trade partners to corner the market in impossible things. Beat: revelation; the hunt isn't fear—it's profit.

chapters.title: What the Stone Asks
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the covenant-stone, Mirabel learns renewal requires a cartographer's true name freely given—meaning he can never hide again, in either realm. He hesitates. Beat: the central choice crystallized: invisibility or integrity.

chapters.title: The Unraveling
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The covenant fails early: coastlines in both realms blur, streets dissolve into sketches, people fade where they were never truly remembered. Beat: catastrophe; delay is no longer an option.

chapters.title: Return Through Burning Pages
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel fights back across the thinning border, guided by the Warden's sacrifice, and emerges in the guild's ruined map-room just as Corvane orders it burned. Beat: homecoming inverted—the safe place is now the battlefield.

chapters.title: The Ledger Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Sela, alternating. Before the surviving guild and arriving Veilwardens, Sela reads Corvane's sold-names ledger aloud while Mirabel displays the archivist's proof. The wardens waver. Beat: climax of truth; loyalty to people triumphs over loyalty to institution.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Corvane, exposed, attempts to destroy the covenant-stone's anchor rather than let the guild fall. Mirabel stops him—not with force, but by mapping Corvane honestly, showing him the man he became. Beat: defeat without caricature; Corvane breaks.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the stone, Mirabel speaks his true name and signs the new covenant in blood and ink, binding both realms openly. The pain nearly kills him; the Warden's lingering hand steadies his own. Beat: sacrificial climax; the price paid willingly.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Weeks later, the guild reopens under new charter: no more selling names, every gift registered to protect, not to hunt. Sela becomes its keeper of truths. Beat: resolution; institutions can be reforged when someone pays the cost.

chapters.title: Ivo and the Veil
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel publishes his first honest map under his own name, titled 'Ivo and the Veil'—Ivo being the name his mother gave him, restored along with the memory he sacrificed. Beat: belonging earned; invisible no more, and at peace with the price.
